new_incident_text: Robot BOT-OPS-05 has faulted after each of the last several transactions in the DocumentValidation queue. In every case the transaction's core processing completes successfully and the output file is written correctly, but the robot then throws an unhandled exception during a cleanup step immediately afterward, before the queue item can be marked Successful. The queue item is left stuck In Progress every time, and this has now repeated across several consecutive runs, not just once.
Our SAP automation fails clicking Save on the ME21N screen with an 'element not found' error. It was working fine until a recent SAP client patch went out.

A process automating one of our internal web portals suddenly can't find a button it used to click, with no error in our own code — looks like the button just isn't where it used to be after the site got a recent UI update.

A customer emailed complaining that the invoice PDF we sent had the wrong currency symbol in the letterhead branding — nothing to do with any automation failing, just a design/content mistake in the template.

A customer emailed complaining that the invoice PDF we sent had the wrong currency symbol in the letterhead branding — nothing to do with any automation failing, just a design/content mistake in the template.

A client flagged that the currency sign printed on the header of the invoice PDFs we generate looks wrong - doesn't seem like anything failed on the automation side, more like a mistake in the document template itself.

Our invoice process's 'Invalid vendor ID' validation failures are getting retried three times before escalating as a system error, instead of logging once as a clean business exception like they should.

One of our finance web app automations keeps breaking on the Submit button every single time there's a new release - not once, but basically every deploy cycle, which feels different from a one-off redesign.

Robot BOT-FIN-07 went offline in Orchestrator overnight during the nightly finance batch and queue items were left In Progress again - this isn't the first time something like this has happened this month.
An employee wants to know the company's policy on carrying over unused annual leave into the next calendar year.
